lead: At least 37 suspected oil thieves died after inhaling fumes while loading stolen product at a jetty in Okrika, Rivers State. A Federal High Court ordered that the jailed head of a fake investment council be allowed to see his lawyers, and the Presidency said the US case involving President Tinubu is not a criminal trial. Ten Nigerian companies joined FTSE Russell's frontier index, business activity grew for a third month, and Peter Obi said he was ready to die protecting his votes.

items.h: At least 37 suspected oil thieves die at Okrika jetty
items.s: Police in Rivers State confirmed that suspected oil thieves died after inhaling fumes while loading a petroleum product into boats at Okari Jetty, Okrika, early on Thursday. Reported death tolls ranged from 37 to 43, and Indorama-Eleme Petrochemicals opened its own investigation.

items.h: Court orders police and AGF to let fake council chief see lawyers
items.s: A Federal High Court in Abuja ordered the Inspector-General of Police and the Attorney-General to give Adeniyi Adeyemi, who styled himself head of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council, access to his lawyers. The court refused his requests for release and bail.

items.h: House panel finds 12 fake bodies linked to Adeyemi and clears Gbajabiamila
items.s: The House of Representatives committee on the council said it uncovered 12 fake agencies, companies and foundations tied to Adeyemi. Its chairman, Yusuf Gadgi, said Femi Gbajabiamila was not questioned because the inquiry's mandate was how the body came into existence.

items.h: Presidency says Tinubu's US court case is not a criminal trial
items.s: The Presidency said the US case is about whether redactions by the FBI and DEA in documents released under freedom of information rules are lawful. A House deputy spokesman said the opposition's campaign over the documents damages Nigeria's image abroad.

items.h: Dangote says reforms are lifting the economy and investor confidence
items.s: Aliko Dangote, president of Dangote Industries, said the government's fiscal, monetary and regulatory reforms have improved macroeconomic stability and strengthened investor confidence.

items.h: Ten Nigerian stocks added to FTSE Russell frontier index
items.s: FTSE Russell included Dangote Cement, MTN, Zenith, GTCO, First HoldCo, Aradel and four others in its frontier index series as Nigeria returns to frontier market status from 21 September after three years.

items.h: Business activity expands for third month as PMI rises to 52.7
items.s: The Central Bank's composite purchasing managers' index rose to 52.7 in August from 51.1 in July, its third straight month above 50, driven by services and agriculture.

items.h: Plateau governor convenes security council over attacks and killings
items.s: Governor Caleb Mutfwang summoned the State Security Council, including heads of security agencies, to review recent attacks and strengthen measures to protect lives and property in Plateau.

items.h: Obi says he is ready to die protecting his votes
items.s: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, told a town hall meeting in Port Harcourt that he was prepared to lose his life defending his votes in 2027 and urged Nigerians to prevent a repeat of past irregularities.

items.h: INEC considers mock presidential election before 2027
items.s: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission may stage a mock presidential poll to test voter accreditation and result transmission under election-day conditions. INEC is also preparing to counter AI-driven disinformation.

items.h: Fubara signs his first budget as Rivers governor after long crisis
items.s: Governor Siminalayi Fubara signed a budget at Government House, Port Harcourt, the first he has assented to since taking office in 2023, Premium Times reported.

items.h: Uber launches robotaxi rides in London a day after leaving Nigeria
items.s: Uber and British AI company Wayve unveiled autonomous rides in London, Reuters reported, less than 24 hours after Uber ended its ride-hailing service in Nigeria.

items.h: ADC says Uber's exit shows Nigeria is becoming a graveyard of businesses
items.s: The African Democratic Congress blamed President Tinubu's economic policies for Uber's departure and for other international firms scaling down in Nigeria.

items.h: AAUA students protest 68-day strike
items.s: Students of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, blocked the main gate and nearby roads on Thursday to demand an end to a strike that has halted academic work for 68 days.

items.h: CAN warns politicians against using Jesus Christ for partisan ends
items.s: Christian Association of Nigeria president Archbishop Daniel Okoh told politicians and supporters to stop drawing the name of Jesus Christ into election campaigns ahead of 2027.

items.h: Shettima unveils national land transport policy
items.s: Vice President Kashim Shettima launched a national land transport policy in Abuja aimed at a safer and better integrated transport system, at the 19th National Council on Transportation.

items.h: Emir of Gumel dies in Egypt
items.s: The Emir of Gumel in Jigawa State, Alhaji Ahmed Muhammad Sani II, died on Thursday in Egypt.

items.h: Tinubu mourns Emir of Zurmi
items.s: President Tinubu expressed sorrow at the death of the Emir of Zurmi, Alhaji Bello Sulaiman, who died on Monday five years after ascending the throne.

items.h: Army rescues abducted wife of retired general and arrests kidnappers
items.s: Troops of the Guards Brigade rescued the wife of retired Brigadier General Basil Adonkie, who was abducted from her home on 1 September, and arrested suspects, the army said.

items.h: Troops kill suspected bandit on Benue road
items.s: Operation Whirl Stroke said its soldiers shot dead a suspected bandit during a patrol in Katsina-Ala and recovered a weapon and ammunition.

items.h: Troops seize 899 rounds of ammunition in North-West raids
items.s: Operation Fansan Yamma said soldiers killed several terrorists and seized 899 rounds of ammunition in Zamfara and Kaduna on Wednesday.

items.h: Defence minister says motorcycle palliatives end up with terrorists
items.s: Defence Minister Christopher Musa warned governors and lawmakers against handing out motorcycles as palliatives, saying some end up used by terrorists.

items.h: Bauchi senator's banditry allegations prompt calls for DSS probe
items.s: Allegations against Shehu Buba Umar, who represents Bauchi South, have stirred controversy across the North and led to calls for an investigation by the Department of State Services, BusinessDay reported.

items.h: Police show of force at Abuja flashpoints ahead of 2027
items.s: FCT police staged a show of force at identified flashpoints in the capital. INEC has fixed 16 January 2027 for the presidential election.

items.h: Wike orders investigation into Airport Road and Lokogoma floods
items.s: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike set up a task force to find the causes of recent flooding along the Airport Road axis and in Lokogoma and propose lasting solutions.

items.h: Marwa tells NDLEA to go after drug cartels' money
items.s: NDLEA chairman Buba Marwa directed investigators and prosecutors to trace and seize traffickers' proceeds, saying arrests and seizures alone will not defeat the cartels.

items.h: Judge returns Awujale succession suit for reassignment
items.s: A vacation judge at the Ogun State High Court in Ijebu-Ode sent back the suit over the selection of the next Awujale for reassignment. The Fusengbuwa ruling house filed the case in August.

items.h: Assault on doctor triggers fresh strike at UUTH
items.s: Doctors at the University of Uyo Teaching Hospital began another indefinite strike after a colleague was assaulted, months after a similar dispute disrupted services.

items.h: ASUU at Sule Lamido University issues two-week ultimatum over arrears
items.s: The ASUU branch at Sule Lamido University, Kafin Hausa, gave the Jigawa government two weeks to implement the 2025 agreement and pay salary arrears or face a strike.

items.h: NDC rejects INEC's explanation over Anambra candidate list
items.s: The Nigeria Democratic Congress said INEC had not explained how 10 names it did not approve appeared on the commission's portal as its candidates.

items.h: Kaduna backs Tax Ombud as KADIRS credits rise in revenue
items.s: Governor Uba Sani pledged support for the Office of the Tax Ombud to align state tax administration with national reforms. The outgoing head of the Kaduna revenue service said political backing helped raise internally generated revenue.

items.h: Kaduna approves higher pay and security allowances for traditional rulers
items.s: Kaduna's information commissioner announced that emirs, chiefs and district and village heads across the state's three senatorial zones will receive better pay, along with new security allowances.

items.h: NPA to take over inland dry ports from Shippers' Council
items.s: The Federal Government directed the Nigerian Ports Authority to assume the inland dry port functions previously handled by the Nigerian Shippers' Council.

items.h: Cash outside banks falls to N4.8trn, an eight-month low
items.s: Central Bank data showed currency outside banks fell 2.4 per cent to N4.8 trillion in July 2026, its lowest since November 2025.

items.h: Brent nears $97 as Iran keeps up strikes on Gulf states
items.s: Brent crude rose to $96.98 a barrel as Iran continued attacks on US allies in the Gulf, and Nigerian marketers reviewed petrol prices.

items.h: IEA chief says energy investment in Nigeria could double in five years
items.s: International Energy Agency executive director Fatih Birol said investment in Nigeria's energy sector could double within five years.

items.h: NNPC oil output falls to 1.68m barrels a day in July
items.s: NNPC Limited's July report showed crude and condensate production dropped to 1.68 million barrels a day from 1.73 million in May.

items.h: House committee tells DisCos to clear electricity market debts
items.s: The House Committee on Power urged indebted distribution companies to settle their market obligations, warning that defaults threaten the sector's finances.

items.h: Kogi plans N8.55bn social support for 281,750 people
items.s: The Kogi State Government proposed an N8.55 billion social investment package covering about 281,750 beneficiaries in all 21 local government areas.

items.h: FCT begins free rabies vaccination for up to 20,000 dogs and cats
items.s: The FCT Administration started a two-week rabies vaccination campaign across the six area councils, targeting 15,000 to 20,000 pets.

items.h: Bauchi repairs storm-damaged girls' school hostels
items.s: Work to restore storm-damaged hostels at the government girls' secondary school in Tafawa Balewa is about 80 per cent done, Bauchi's education commissioner said after an inspection.

items.h: Ebonyi police arrest 620 suspects and recover 31 guns
items.s: The Ebonyi State Police Command said it arrested 620 suspects over 372 reported cases and recovered 31 firearms.

items.h: Six arrested over fake euro notes in Oyo
items.s: Oyo police arrested six suspects linked to producing and circulating counterfeit euro notes and recovered €8,900 in fakes.

items.h: Police arrest suspected kidnappers terrorising Edo North
items.s: Edo police said suspects accused of kidnappings around Auchi and Okpella were arrested in Niger State by anti-kidnapping units.

items.h: Nomba raises $3m debt facility for Africa-Asia payments
items.s: Lagos fintech Nomba raised a $3 million debt facility through CardinalStone Finance to expand cross-border payments between Africa and Asia.

items.h: NBC chief says audience data is key to digital switchover
items.s: National Broadcasting Commission director-general Charles Ebuebu described reliable audience measurement as the new currency of broadcasting as Nigeria moves to digital television.

items.h: Sanwo-Olu inaugurates 44 sports association chairmen ahead of Eko 2026
items.s: Lagos Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu swore in chairmen of 44 sports associations and said the National Intermediate Games will showcase grassroots talent.

items.h: Germany sanctions Russia over Leipzig drone attack
items.s: Germany closed Russia's consulate in Bonn and tightened controls on Russian nationals after what it called a hybrid drone attack on Leipzig airport.
